summary:
Radar for 1 Oct 2026, with EASD 2026 (Milan, 28 Sep–2 Oct) and EADV 2026 (Vienna, 30 Sep–3 Oct) running at once. I checked 10 of these topics with web searches.

**Best openings right now:**
1. **GLP-1 and nail detachment:** 39% of users vs 9% of comparable non-users (EADV). It's a new side-effect question that fits next to our hair-loss content, and creators haven't covered it yet.
2. **Headline decoders for this week's "X beat Y" claims:**
   - EloraTZP vs tirzepatide 15 mg: a Phase 2 trial, and 10.8–27% of people on EloraTZP stopped because of side effects, vs 2.9% on tirzepatide.
   - Zepbound vs Wegovy HD: an indirect comparison. The gap was statistically significant under one way of counting and not under the other.
   - Ozempic 2 mg vs switching to Mounjaro: an observational study paid for by Novo.
3. **Keeping muscle on GLP-1:** Regeneron's trevogrumab plus semaglutide cut lean-mass loss from 6.7% to 3.3% at 26 weeks. It's still experimental, and two people died in a different, higher-dose combination arm.
4. **Newer topics still at the early stage:**
   - Real-world weight loss after switching from injections to the Wegovy pill: 4.1% at 3 months, a retrospective study.
   - STEP UP liver fat: 8.8% down to 3.1%, a post hoc subgroup of 55 people.
   - A pregnancy-safety meta-analysis: 7 studies, more than 43,000 people exposed.
   - Orforglipron heart safety vs insulin glargine (ACHIEVE-4).

**Ageing topics:**
- Retatrutide and "metabolic whiplash" after stopping are now peaking. Only cover them by decoding the headline numbers.
- The SELECT mediation story is fading (its score fell from 72 to 50), so I've dropped it.

**Rejected:** "Microdosing GLP-1s" (Yahoo Creators) and anything about "research-grade" peptides. Both are against our guardrails.

**Two cautions for the next steps:**
- Several candidates come from company press releases or post hoc analyses. Downstream agents should use the paper's own wording, with comparators and absolute numbers.
- ACHIEVE-4 overlaps with a Short already made on 10-01. Only use it with a new angle.

candidates.topic: GLP-1 users had nail detachment 4x more often: 39% vs 9% in metabolically similar non-users (first controlled study, EADV Congress 2026)
candidates.angle: Search-style question: 'Do GLP-1s (Ozempic, Mounjaro) make your nails fall off?' Give the real numbers: 39% vs 9% for detachment, 46% vs 17% for discolouration. Then give the honest limits: the study can't show cause, about half of users had nail problems before starting, and after adjusting the link was about 2–3x. Link it to the evidence that hair loss is usually temporary and tied to rapid weight loss, and give gentle habits: protein (unless your clinician has told you to limit it), and see a clinician about nail changes. Close with the prescriber line.
candidates.why_now: Presented 30 Sep at EADV and picked up within 24 hours by HCPLive, Medical Xpress, HealthDay and US News. It's a new, visual side effect that people will search for. Our hair-loss long-form was in our top 2, and creators haven't covered this yet.

evidence.signal: First controlled study: nail detachment 39% vs 9%; discolouration 46% vs 17%; can't establish cause; about 2–3x after adjustment
Clinician outlet coverage, 1 Oct
Mainstream pickup 1 Oct: 'Odds of losing your nails, hair rise'

candidates.topic: Did EloraTZP (eloralintide + tirzepatide) really beat Zepbound? 13.2–23.3% vs 14.8% weight loss at 48 weeks in adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity/overweight (Phase 2b, n=367, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: Headline decoder: 'Did Lilly's new combo really beat tirzepatide (Zepbound/Mounjaro)?' The answer is yes at higher dose tiers, but the range starts below tirzepatide. It's a Phase 2 trial, and 10.8–27.0% stopped because of side effects vs 2.9% on tirzepatide. Explain amylin as a third fullness hormone. It isn't approved; Phase 3 is planned (as of Oct 2026).
keywords: new weight loss drug better than Zepbound
candidates.why_now: In our snapshots twice (90, 88). Reuters, CNBC, WSJ, STAT and Fierce covered it 30 Sep–1 Oct, and the 'beats Zepbound' framing is spreading. It matches our best 'Did X really beat Y?' title pattern (the CagriSema Short got 1.8x median), and the side-effect trade-off is under-reported.

evidence.signal: Weight loss 13.2–23.3% vs tirzepatide 14.8%; stopped for side effects 10.8–27.0% vs 2.9%
EASD 2026 trial summary
Company release with the full arms

candidates.topic: Did Zepbound really beat Wegovy HD (semaglutide 7.2 mg)? Lilly's indirect comparison: 4.5 percentage points more weight loss at 72 weeks, significant under only one way of counting
candidates.angle: Headline decoder that teaches people how to read a trial: separate trials (SURMOUNT-1 vs STEP UP), no head-to-head study, and a Lilly-sponsored analysis. The gap was significant counting 'everyone randomised' (treatment-regimen) but not 'if they stayed on treatment' (efficacy estimand). Takeaway: both are effective, and the choice is a conversation with your prescriber. No switching advice.
keywords: which is better Zepbound or Wegovy
candidates.why_now: Lilly's press release came out 29 Sep at EASD. 'Zepbound vs Wegovy' is a steady search with very high volume, and the new Wegovy HD dose gives it a fresh hook. Coverage so far is mostly brand and press-release pages, with little independent explanation.

evidence.signal: Tirzepatide 15 mg 4.5% and 10 mg 3.2% more weight loss vs semaglutide 7.2 mg (treatment-regimen estimand)
Not statistically significant under the efficacy estimand; separate trials
Separate independent indirect comparison of tirzepatide vs semaglutide in people without type 2 diabetes (28 Sep)

candidates.topic: A muscle-protecting add-on? Regeneron's trevogrumab with semaglutide cut lean-mass loss from 6.7% to 3.3% at 26 weeks (Phase 2)
candidates.angle: 'Can you keep muscle on a GLP-1?' Open with the new trial number (an experimental antibody that blocks myostatin, not approved). Then pivot to what works today: protein (unless your clinician has told you to limit it, e.g. kidney disease) and strength training. Be honest that two deaths led Regeneron to drop a separate higher-dose triple combination with garetosmab.
keywords: how to keep muscle on Ozempic
candidates.why_now: Reuters covered it 30 Sep, with follow-ups from Medical Xpress and EMJ on 1 Oct. Muscle loss is one of the biggest GLP-1 worries and on our double-down list. A Clin Nutr piece on creatine for GLP-1-associated muscle loss also appeared this week.

evidence.signal: Lean-mass loss 6.7% on semaglutide alone vs 3.3% with trevogrumab 75 mg over 26 weeks
Triple combination dropped after two deaths; study planned in adults over 65
'Creatine for GLP-1-associated muscle loss' (21 Sep)

candidates.topic: Switching from GLP-1 injections to the Wegovy pill: 4.1% further average weight loss at 3 months (OCTANE real-world data, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: 'Does the Wegovy pill work as well as the shot?' Explain what OCTANE was: a retrospective study of telehealth patients who switched from injectable semaglutide or tirzepatide, presented by Novo, with no comparison group. 40.7% lost a further 5% or more. Compare with the pill's trial data and tell people to talk to their prescriber before any switch. Don't name or promote the telehealth platform.
candidates.why_now: CNBC, Reuters and IBTimes covered it 30 Sep–1 Oct. Interest in pills is high (Everyday Health ran '8 misconceptions about oral GLP-1s' on 1 Oct), and our orforglipron content got our best long-form views.

evidence.signal: 4.1% average weight loss at 3 months after switching; presented at EASD2026
Retrospective cohort of telehealth patients who switched 5 Jan–7 Feb 2026; 40.7% reached 5% or more

candidates.topic: Semaglutide brought liver fat down from 8.8% to 3.1% at 72 weeks in adults with obesity; 23 of 26 with excess liver fat reached normal levels (STEP UP exploratory subgroup, n=55)
candidates.angle: Benefits beyond weight: 'Can Wegovy (semaglutide) reverse fatty liver?' Explain fatty liver (MASLD/MASH) simply, give the subgroup numbers with clear caveats (post hoc, not a planned endpoint, 55 people, no diabetes), and point to the stronger evidence base (ESSENCE / the MASH approval).
candidates.why_now: Novo's release on 1 Oct, picked up by Yahoo and Stock Titan. Fatty liver is common in our audience and searched year-round, and this gives it a fresh, concrete number.

evidence.signal: Liver fat 8.8% to 3.1% at week 72; 9 of 10 with excess liver fat reached normal
Subgroup of 55; exploratory; not a pre-specified endpoint

candidates.topic: GLP-1 exposure in pregnancy not linked to major adverse pregnancy outcomes in women with diabetes (meta-analysis, 7 studies, 43,000+ exposed; Lancet Obstet Gynaecol Women's Health, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: Reassuring but careful: 'Is it dangerous if you got pregnant on Ozempic?' Explain what was found (no significant association with preterm birth, stillbirth, pre-eclampsia and other outcomes, in women with diabetes) and the evidence gaps the authors flag. Labelling still says to stop before a planned pregnancy, so talk to your prescriber as early as possible. Don't tell anyone to stop or keep taking medication.
candidates.why_now: News-Medical and Nutrition Insight covered it 1 Oct, alongside a French nationwide Diabetologia study (29 Sep). 'Ozempic babies' is a long-running social search, and Medical Xpress flags that women are the main users while research gaps remain.

evidence.signal: 7 studies, more than 43,000 exposed; no significant associations with major adverse outcomes
'Appear safe ... but evidence gaps remain'
French nationwide study on GLP-1 safety in pregnancy with type 2 diabetes

candidates.topic: Retatrutide headlines decoded: '50 pounds', 'up to 60 pounds', '30%'. What TRIUMPH-2 (Lancet) actually showed: up to 20.8% average weight loss at 80 weeks vs 4.0% placebo in adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity
candidates.angle: Headline decoder: 'Does retatrutide really cause 30% weight loss?' Separate the trials and populations (TRIUMPH-2 in type 2 diabetes vs other TRIUMPH obesity data), the dose arms, average vs 'up to', and the side effects analysts flagged. Not FDA-approved (as of Oct 2026). Warn clearly against 'research-grade' sellers without naming any.
candidates.why_now: Published in The Lancet 29 Sep. USA Today, NBC, Time, CBS, Scientific American and the Guardian all covered it, with conflicting numbers. Demand is peaking, so only a decoder that untangles the numbers stands out.

evidence.signal: TRIUMPH-2 Phase 3 paper
Full Phase 3 data
Analysts concerned about side effects (TRIUMPH-1)

candidates.topic: Is the daily GLP-1 pill safe for the heart? Orforglipron (Foundayo) met non-inferiority vs insulin glargine for major heart events (ACHIEVE-4, Lancet; HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.59–1.20)
candidates.angle: Explain 'non-inferior' in plain English: it means not worse, not 'better'. Then cover the A1C results (65.7% vs 46.0% reached HbA1c under 7%) and the 10.6% who stopped because of side effects. Treat the all-cause death signal as nominal and exploratory, with absolute rates. It's a new angle vs our 10-01 Short: a 'pill vs insulin' explainer for people with type 2 diabetes.
candidates.why_now: Lancet paper 30 Sep, with MedPage, Healio and HCPLive coverage. A Lilly release on 1 Oct adds modelled long-term risk claims (modelled, not measured, so use with care). Overlaps with S3 10-01, so a distinct angle is needed.

evidence.signal: MACE HR 0.84 (0.59–1.20); all-cause death HR 0.43 nominal
Company release
ACHIEVE-4 paper

candidates.topic: Do GLP-1s cause pancreatic cancer? Nordic registry (97,464 matched pairs) plus a new global propensity-matched cohort in type 2 diabetes found no increased risk
candidates.angle: Myth-check in a positive tone, answering the exact search 'does tirzepatide/semaglutide cause cancer'. Give both studies' populations, say they're observational, and note what remains unknown. Mention pancreatitis warning symptoms with urgency: severe tummy pain spreading to the back means call 911/999.
candidates.why_now: Steady in 5 snapshots (about 80). Medscape covered it 28 Sep, a new J Pers Med cohort is out, and 'does tirzepatide cause cancer' appears as a live search query in our signals.

evidence.signal: Semaglutide not linked to higher pancreatic cancer risk
Global propensity-matched cohort: no increased pancreatitis or pancreatic cancer risk

candidates.topic: Stopping GLP-1s and heart risk: up to 22% higher risk of heart attack, stroke and death after 2 years off (BMJ Medicine, 333,000+ US veterans with type 2 diabetes, observational)
candidates.angle: Differentiated, non-scary angle: 'Thinking of stopping? Questions to ask your prescriber first.' Give the population and that it's observational, use 'linked to', and include absolute context if the paper gives it. Focus on planning with a clinician, never on stop/keep advice.
keywords: what happens when you stop GLP-1
candidates.why_now: Still circulating (Scripps News and Yahoo Creators on 1 Oct), but the score is falling across 5 snapshots (84 to 74). Only worth doing as a calm 'plan with your doctor' piece.

evidence.signal: Coverage 1 Oct

candidates.topic: Ozempic 2 mg vs switching to Mounjaro: Novo's real-world analysis linked staying on and increasing semaglutide to lower heart-event risk than switching to tirzepatide in type 2 diabetes (EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: Pair it with the Lilly comparison: 'Both companies say they won. Here's how to read rival studies.' It's an observational, company-sponsored study with possible confounding, and SURPASS-CVOT is the randomised evidence. Absolutely no switching advice.
candidates.why_now: Novo's release on 29 Sep, plus HCPLive and Cardiovascular Business coverage. Works well as a media-literacy decoder next to Lilly's indirect comparison.

evidence.signal: Increasing to semaglutide 2 mg linked to lower heart-event risk than switching to tirzepatide in type 2 diabetes
SURPASS-CVOT randomised comparison (tirzepatide vs dulaglutide) for context

candidates.topic: GLP-1s in children and teens with type 2 diabetes: use rose from 6.3% to 27.2% (2019–2025) in a German/Austrian/Luxembourg registry, plus a STAT 'results are reassuring' opinion
candidates.angle: For parents: what the evidence says about GLP-1s for young people with type 2 diabetes or obesity. Give the approval context by age, the registry numbers, and what's still unknown. Only for parents of children prescribed these medicines, and talk to the paediatric team.
candidates.why_now: Covered 30 Sep–1 Oct by STAT, News-Medical, ABC30 and CBS19. Parents aged 25–65 are in our audience.

evidence.signal: 1,878 young people aged 6–24 with type 2 diabetes; use 6.3% (2019) to 27.2% (2025)
Opinion: 'I studied GLP-1 use in children. The results are reassuring'

candidates.topic: Ozempic, Wegovy and Rybelsus US list prices drop to $675 from 1 Jan 2027 (up to 50% lower), and why cost affects whether people stay on treatment
candidates.angle: 'Will GLP-1s get cheaper in 2027?' Explain list price vs out-of-pocket cost, who benefits (high-deductible and coinsurance plans), the negotiated Medicare price, and the new UGA data showing higher costs lead to lower adherence. Point people to legitimate prescription routes only.
candidates.predicted_peak: recurring; spikes toward Jan 2027 and open enrolment (Nov)
candidates.why_now: Back in the news (Medical Economics, 1 Oct), alongside UGA adherence data and coverage-shift equity stories. US Medicare open enrolment starts 15 Oct.

evidence.signal: List price cut to $675 from 2027
Wegovy 50%, Ozempic 35% lower

candidates.topic: Nausea, constipation and other stomach side effects on GLP-1s: a new expert review covering approved injections, pills and pipeline drugs (Nutr Clin Pract, Oct 2026)
candidates.angle: Practical 'make it easier' piece: how common the stomach side effects are, why they cluster when the dose goes up, and habits with evidence behind them (smaller meals, eat slowly, stop at fullness, fibre, fluids unless you've been told to limit fluids). Include red flags. No dosing advice.
keywords: how to stop nausea on Wegovy
candidates.why_now: New review published, and the EloraTZP and retatrutide side-effect headlines bring the topic back up. It's one of the most searched GLP-1 questions.

evidence.signal: Expert narrative review of GLP-1 and GIP/GLP-1 stomach side effects

candidates.topic: Creatine for GLP-1-associated muscle loss: what the evidence does and doesn't show (Clin Nutr 2026)
candidates.angle: Search-style question: 'Should you take creatine on Ozempic?' Be honest: there's no GLP-1-specific trial evidence yet. Creatine plus resistance training has evidence in older adults. Talk to your clinician, especially with kidney disease. Strength training and protein come first.
keywords: creatine muscle loss weight loss drugs
candidates.why_now: Clin Nutr piece on 21 Sep, plus the Regeneron muscle news. Creatine is trending in wellness circles.

evidence.signal: 'Creatine for GLP-1-associated muscle loss' (not yet checked: probably a commentary or review, not a trial)

candidates.topic: Fewer migraine meds after starting semaglutide: triptan use fell after people started semaglutide for weight loss (Clinical Pain Advisor report)
candidates.angle: Promising early research, framed honestly: an observational signal in medication use, not proof that semaglutide treats migraine. Explain the brain-pressure hypothesis carefully and say trials are needed.
candidates.why_now: Report published 30 Sep. Few creators have covered it. Not yet checked against the primary paper.

evidence.signal: Triptan use falls after starting semaglutide for weight loss
